newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajiks seize U.N., Red Cross workers, journalists.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks seize U.N., Red Cross workers, journalists.

text.p: A group of Tajik rebels which seized four U.N. observers earlier this week has detained four Russian reporters and two Red Cross workers who went to investigate the kidnapping, a U.N. spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We have radio contact with our people and we have information that four journalists have been detained," the spokesman said.

The U.N. spokesman said a foreign employee of the International Red Cross and an interpreter bringing medical aid to one of the military observers were also seized. He gave no further details as to the identity of the Red Cross workers.
The U.N. has demanded the immediate release of the observers, an Austrian, a Ukrainian, two Swiss nationals and an interpreter. It says that the Austrian is seriously ill.
The group of reporters, two men and two women, were heading for the rebel district when they were captured.

The reporters had been planning to rendevous with an armed group led by Rizvon Sadirov, who once fought for the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition against the secular government but whose loyalties now are unclear.
Sadirov's group captured the U.N. personnel on Tuesday about four km (two miles) from the town of Obigarm in the centre of the remote, mountainous republic.
The group is demanding safe passage for its members based in neighbouring Afghanistan back into the former Soviet republic.

The United Nations Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) has about 45 military personnel in the republic to observe a fragile peace agreement aimed at ending a bitter four-year civil war between the secular government and Islamist opposition forces.
A ceasefire agreed between the government and the guerrillas has held for nearly two months and further peace talks are due to be held on February 26 in Moscow.
Last December, Sadirov's group took 23 people hostage, including seven U.N. observers, to demand the release of his brother. All the hostages were later released.
